newsitem.title: USA: U.S. leases St James oil terminal to Shell.
newsitem.headline: U.S. leases St James oil terminal to Shell.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said Friday it had signed an agreement to lease its St. James, Louisiana oil terminal and a 37-mile long pipeline to Shell Pipe Line Corp, a subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell.
Based on Shell's usage projections, the government expects to collect $5 million to $8 million a year from the lease agreement within the next four years.
The government also agreed to sell its 67-mile long Weeks Island pipeline for $22 million to Louisiana Intrastate Gas Co, an Equitable Resources Inc company.
Louisiana Intrastate is expected to take over ownership of the pipeline within seven months, as soon as the government has finished moving oil out of its damaged Weeks Island storage site.

The St. James terminal on the Mississippi River, the 37-mile pipeline to the Energy Department's Bayou Choctaw oil storage site, and the Weeks Island pipeline are all part of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve system.
Under the terms of the lease to Shell, the government will be allowed to use the pipeline and terminal if it has to draw down crude from the oil reserve during an energy emergency.
The underused facilities were put up for lease or sale this year, after a similar effort in 1994 failed.
The Energy Department said the main reason industry expressed more interest in the offer this time is because the solicitation document had been pared down to three pages from 100 pages.
